claims.text: WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain relative to pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing service.
WTaTiVZr has enhanced toughness relative to pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing service.
The enhanced plastic strain and toughness are governed by a refined, homogeneous microstructure.
WTaTiVZr contains stable intergranular secondary-phase precipitates.
The intergranular secondary-phase precipitates mediate dislocation motion.
The refined grain structure and secondary phases pin dislocations at lower strains.
At higher temperatures, the secondary phases act as sources for dislocation generation.
The proposed balance between dislocation pinning and generation reduces brittle-crack initiation.
The proposed balance between dislocation pinning and generation enhances ductility and toughness.
Pure tungsten lacks the microstructural refinement proposed for WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit significantly greater plastic strain than pure tungsten in high-temperature tests.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher fracture toughness than pure tungsten in high-temperature tests.
WTaTiVZr will show smaller and more homogeneous grains than pure tungsten.
Temperatures above 1200 degrees Celsius are representative of plasma-facing-component service for the proposed comparison.
The hypothesized benefit may diminish above the stability range of the refined microstructure.
High-flux irradiation or oxidative environments may alter the microstructural balance in WTaTiVZr.

contradictions.description: The initial state and baseline describe commercially processed pure tungsten, whereas the intervention and falsification design call for pure tungsten prepared by the same arc-melting and repeated-remelting protocol as WTaTiVZr. These are different baseline states and make the intended control ambiguous.
